reasons: Classification is correct: Article 15 contains only Effective-Date representations plus a blanket disclaimer of implied warranties (p0711), with no ongoing performance warranty, no conformance warranty for Materials supplied under Article 9, and no repair/replace/refund remedy — this fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so it is a genuine deviation rather than an acceptable fallback being upgraded.
Rule kind and detection guidance expressly treat a missing express warranty as a deviation to be cured by insertion, so the insert-based approach is appropriate and actionable.

The inserted 15.4 reaches the playbook position: professional/workmanlike standard, material conformance of supplied Materials to specifications/GMP, compliance with law, no malicious code, and a re-perform/replace/refund remedy at Array's option — matching the model language and adapted sensibly to a pharma supply context.

The failed deterministic check on warranty duration is a phrasing variant only: the text does contain a ninety (90) day notice window measured from delivery, with a latent-defect extension, which satisfies the ≥90-day parameter.

Edit footprint is proportionate — the only change to existing text is renumbering 15.4 to 15.5 (changed-character ratio 0.032), and no disclaimer carve-out is needed because p0711 already opens with 'Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement', as the comment accurately states.

Minor, non-disqualifying points to check on execution: subsequent Article 15 section numbers and any cross-references may also need renumbering, and the inserted clause relies on defined terms (Materials, Good Manufacturing Practices, Law, Development/Manufacturing) that should be confirmed as defined in the Agreement; the 'software or electronic deliverables' limb is largely inapposite here but harmless.
